scope: A bounded performance audit of exact library operations used by homological-conjectures; no consumer API migration.
changes: Share immutable Groebner relation storage; lazily reuse tip dictionaries, nontips, and canonical coordinate ordering. Tail reduction uses copy-on-write and changed tips get fresh caches.
Reuse the right Groebner basis locally across generators in each GSZ resolution step, preserving checks and error order.
Skip zero and unit arithmetic during matrix products; nullspace queries no longer materialize unused dense basis and transformation outputs.
Compare immutable module representations without cloning arrow matrices, with a direct identity shortcut.
Compose validated immutable maps without repeating arrow-square validation. Public construction still checks every entered matrix; exact composition preserves the checked invariants.

inventory.method: AST scan of lib and experiments Python files that directly import qpa; attribute call counts are syntactic, not type-resolved or runtime frequencies.
inventory.limitations: This is a workload-family audit, not execution of every experiment or coverage of every exposed API.

method.build: Release, default numerica-no-gmp; correctness checks also use numerica-gmp.
method.timing: Five alternating pairs of fresh processes, reversing build order each pair, pinned to CPU 0. One sample per case per process; fresh inputs per case. Existing consumer presentation caches persist within each process. Imports and report output excluded from case timings.
method.comparison: Every returned JSON-normalized result matches baseline. Test-based fixtures returning null execute their original assertions; their null hashes are not complete mathematical certificates.
method.host: Shared WSL2 Linux host. Builds, validation and profiling completed before the accepted comparison. Unrelated consumer work may run concurrently; small timing differences are not reliable speedup claims.
method.profiling: Python cProfile identifies library/consumer boundaries; Callgrind identifies native call costs. Profiled wall times are diagnostic, not benchmark speedups. Native totals include imports; inclusive function counts overlap.
method.provenance: Consumer Cartan tests normally check a different sibling checkout. The survey explicitly redirects that root to the checkout under test via a temporary startup module, also for spawned workers. It preserves real module paths and records extension hashes; consumer source files are unchanged.

commands: PYTHONPATH=<baseline package directory or current python directory> taskset -c 0 .venv/bin/python benchmarks/broad_workloads.py --consumer-root ../homological-conjectures --repeat 1 --output <sample.json> --compare <first-baseline.json>

regressions: Four-field matrix products and nullspace ordering, including empty shapes
Groebner clone sharing, copy-on-write tail reduction, basis replacement and enumerator behavior
GSZ shared-basis overlap results and zero-vector error
Composition versus the checked constructor across four fields, zero spaces and incompatible inputs

assessment.recommendation: End this optimization round and prepare the release.
assessment.stopping_criterion: Investigate substantial costs in representative calculations and retain practical changes with repeatable end-to-end gains; stop when the remaining measured costs require broader algorithm or representation changes, are in consumer orchestration, or are too small to establish a material benefit.
remaining_costs: Large rational Hom calculations still build and eliminate dense exact systems. Sparse or fraction-free approaches would need a separate design preserving QPA basis ordering.

Common-summand calculations still perform the actual Hom searches and matrix products. Specialized matrix layouts or binary multiplication are possible future algorithm work, not measured pending fixes.
Consumer language enumeration, fan geometry, closure search and worker startup are outside the library. Exhaustive module enumeration retains its combinatorial growth.
limits: No claim that all future optimization opportunities are exhausted. Larger or different workloads may reveal new bottlenecks.
Performance comparisons are against the preceding Rust commit, not GAP/QPA, and use one machine and the default backend.
No version bump, tag, publication or cross-platform wheel validation is part of this audit.
assessment.mixed_results: Not every probe improved. The small GF(5) Hom-dimension probe rose from 4.28 ms to 5.94 ms across the accepted repetitions; it also regressed in the earlier pilot. This remains an accepted small absolute regression, not a speedup or a proven noise effect. Other slower medians are recorded in cases; the shared host and run-to-run variation limit interpretation of small differences. The large representative consumer workloads improved materially.
